question: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a severe, chronic and debilitating multisystem disease affecting the nervous, immune and energy metabolism systems. It is characterised by extreme fatigue, cognitive impairment and post-exertional symptom exacerbation. In severe cases, patients are unable to work or leave their homes.

Despite affecting an estimated 40 million people worldwide, it remains one of the least researched chronic conditions, with no causal treatments and significant gaps in diagnosis and care. There is increasing evidence and feedback from across the Member States pointing to persistent shortcomings in research, funding uptake and patient care.
At the same time, it remains unclear as to what extent existing EU funding instruments are effectively utilised for ME/CFS research. In this context: 1.
What specific funding has been allocated and utilised to date under Horizon Europe for research on ME/CFS or closely related conditions?
What measures is the Commission taking to ensure that Member States and research institutions initiate projects relevant to ME/CFS and make use of existing funding opportunities?
Does the Commission plan to launch specific calls for proposals or programmes to strengthen research on ME/CFS?
answer: 1. The Commission does not earmark specific funding for research into myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) under Horizon Europe. However, it proposed in the Horizon Europe Cluster 1 ‘Health’ Work Programme 2025 the call topic ‘Tackling high burden for patients and under-researched medical conditions ’ (1), which is relevant for ME/CFS research.

Similar considerations are being made for the call topic: ‘Advancing research on the prevention, diagnosis, and management of post-infection long-term conditions’ (2) from the Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026-2027 for Cluster 1 ‘Health’.

Additionally, the Commission supports the recently launched European Partnership for Brain Health which should also cater to the needs of researchers working in the area of ME/CFS (3). 2. The Commission recognises the importance of addressing high burden and under- researched medical conditions, including ME/CFS.

It remains committed to funding high-quality proposals across all medical fields, within available budget allocations and in line with strategic priorities agreed together with Member States and associated countries.

In this regard, the Commission is also organising dedicated public Horizon Europe ‘Health’ (Cluster 1) info days (4) and supports the National Contact Points Network (5) to raise awareness of funding opportunities under the forthcoming calls in the Cluster Health work programme. 3.

Subject to the outcome of negotiations on the next Multiannual Financial Framework, the Commission may consider reflecting on proposing call topics in all medical fields, including under-researched medical conditions such as ME/CFS.
